stem: Sam is a 16-month-old infant being discharged after his first episode of salbutamol-responsive wheeze. He will use a spacer at home. Which one of the following pieces of advice about spacer care is correct?

options.text: The dustcap should be replaced between uses
The spacer should be cleaned in warm soapy water once a month and left to air dry
After cleaning, the spacer can also be primed with a number of puffs before use
Delivery devices should not be shared between siblings

explanation: The dustcap should be replaced between uses to keep the inhaler device protected and ready for the next dose. The other options are not standard advice for spacer care in this context.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Part A

rationale: This item is asking for single-best advice on spacer care. Of the options given, replacing the dustcap between uses is the clearest correct instruction.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Replacing the dustcap between uses is appropriate device-care advice.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect. Spacers are typically washed less frequently and left to air dry without rubbing to maintain static properties.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect. Priming with puffs is not routine spacer-care advice after cleaning.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. While personal device use is generally preferred, this is not the best answer to the specific spacer-care question.
